name: W5100S-L
title: W5100S: hardwired TCP/IP Ethernet controller with 10/100 PHY, 4 sockets, 16 KB buffer, SPI or 8-bit bus, LQFP48 / QFN48
summary: A single-chip Ethernet controller that runs the TCP/IP stack in hardware: TCP, UDP, IPv4, ICMP, IGMPv1/v2, ARP, PPPoE and wake-on-LAN over UDP, with an Ethernet MAC and a 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX PHY on board. A host microcontroller drives four independent sockets through registers and a 16 KB packet memory (8 KB transmit, 8 KB receive), over SPI (modes 0 and 3) or an 8-bit parallel bus with two address lines. It runs from 3.3 V with 5 V tolerant I/O, makes its own 1.2 V core supply, and is register compatible with the W5100. W5100S-L is the LQFP48 version and W5100S-Q the QFN48 version, both 7 mm × 7 mm with 0.5 mm pitch.
key_figures: TCP, UDP, IPv4, ICMP, IGMPv1/v2, ARP, PPPoE, WOL over UDP; no IP fragmentation
SPI mode 0/3, 70 MHz design max (33.3 MHz typical tested); or 8-bit parallel bus
2.97 V to 3.63 V (3.3 V typ); internal 1.2 V regulator
93 mA typ at 100M link; 10 mA typ in power-down

rows: Opens the socket in the protocol set in Sn_MR; Sn_SR then reads SOCK_CLOSED (0x00), SOCK_INIT (0x13, TCP), SOCK_UDP (0x22), SOCK_IPRAW (0x32) or SOCK_MACRAW (0x42).

TCP client: sends a SYN to the peer from SOCK_INIT.

Closes the socket (Sn_SR = 0x00); in TCP no FIN is sent.

TCP: sends a keep-alive packet; at least one data byte must have been sent first. No answer within the retransmission time sets TIMEOUT and closes the socket.
Tells the chip the host has read the receive data up to the new Sn_RX_RD.

circuits.title: SPI connection to a host
circuits.description: The host microcontroller is the SPI master and the W5100S the slave. Four wires join them: chip select, clock, and one data line each way. MOD[3:0] are all low for this mode, and the bus runs in SPI mode 0 or 3.

circuits.title: Parallel bus connection to a host
circuits.description: The host drives chip select, read and write strobes and two address lines, and moves bytes on an 8-bit data bus; the W5100S answers its interrupt line back to the host. The two address lines pick MR, the two halves of the offset address, or the data register, which reach every register and buffer byte indirectly. MOD[3:0] = 010X selects this mode.

circuits.title: 25 MHz crystal network
circuits.description: A 25 MHz crystal between XSCI and XSCO with a load capacitor from each side to ground. The 1 MΩ feedback resistor across the two pins is external because the chip has none. A series resistor between XSCO and the crystal limits the power driven into the crystal.

parts.note: load capacitor, usually equal to CL2

notes: CL = (CL1 × CL2) / (CL1 + CL2) + Cs; CL1 is typically equal to CL2. The recommended crystal has CL = 12 pF.

operation.text: Strap MOD[3:0] for the host interface first, then pull RSTn low for longer than 500 ns. After RSTn rises the chip needs TSTA, 60.3 ms, before it is usable. MR[RST] resets all registers from software and clears itself after 3 system clocks. VERR reads 0x51.

Set MR, IMR, RTR and RCR to suit the application; write the MAC address to SHAR, the gateway to GAR, the subnet mask to SUBR and the IP address to SIPR; then size the socket buffers (TMSR and RMSR, or the per-socket Sn_TXBUF_SIZE and Sn_RXBUF_SIZE), keeping each direction's total at 8 KB or less.

With MOD[3:0] = 0000 the chip is an SPI slave in mode 0 or 3: MOSI is sampled on the rising edge of SCLK, MISO changes on the falling edge, most significant bit first. A frame is an 8-bit command (0xF0 write, 0x0F read), a 16-bit address and then any number of data bytes; the address increments after each byte. CSn frames each transfer and stays low for the whole frame; the command starts at least 2 system clocks after CSn falls and CSn rises at least 2 system clocks after the last byte. In SPI mode RDn goes to 3V3D or is left open and DAT[7:0] are left open.

With MOD[3:0] = 010X the host uses CSn, RDn, WRn, ADDR[1:0] and DAT[7:0]. ADDR = 00 reaches MR directly; the host writes the upper and lower offset address to IDM_ARH (01) and IDM_ARL (10), then reads or writes bytes through IDM_DR (11), and the offset steps on for each further byte so a burst needs one address. SCLK is grounded or left open in this mode.

An event sets its bit in IR, IR2, SLIR or Sn_IR. INTn goes low when a set bit's mask (IMR, IMR2, SLIMR, Sn_IMR) is 1, MR2[IEN] is 1 and the INTPTMR pending timer has run out. INTn returns high when the bit is cleared (write 1) or masked.

Each of the four sockets is opened in TCP, UDP, IPRAW or MACRAW mode by writing Sn_MR and issuing OPEN; options in Sn_MR, Sn_MR2 and Sn_MSS are set before OPEN. MACRAW is available on socket 0 only. IP fragmentation is not supported.

A server socket opens in TCP mode, issues LISTEN and waits in SOCK_LISTEN; a client sets Sn_DIPR and Sn_DPORTR and issues CONNECT. Sn_IR[CON] or SOCK_ESTABLISHED marks the connection. Receive: read Sn_RX_RSR bytes from the ring at Sn_RX_RD, advance Sn_RX_RD, issue RECV. Send: write at Sn_TX_WR up to Sn_TX_FSR, advance Sn_TX_WR, issue SEND, wait for SENDOK or TIMEOUT. DISCON closes with a FIN; CLOSE drops the socket at once. Delayed ACK waits RTR or a window change unless Sn_MR[ND] is set; Sn_MR2[BRDB] forces PSH on every segment.

A keep-alive packet carries the last byte already sent, so at least one byte of data must go first. Sn_KPALVTR sends one every value × 5 s; with it at zero, SEND_KEEP sends one on demand. No answer within the retransmission time sets Sn_IR[TIMEOUT].

A UDP socket talks to many peers without connections. Each received datagram is stored behind an 8-byte header: peer IP (4 bytes), peer port (2) and data length (2). A datagram larger than the free receive space is dropped. Before sending to a new peer the socket runs ARP; a TIMEOUT from ARP does not close a UDP socket. SEND_MAC with Sn_DHAR set skips ARP. MR2[FARP] forces ARP before every datagram.
Set Sn_MR[MULTI], choose IGMP version 2 or 1 with Sn_MR[MC], and load Sn_DHAR, Sn_DIPR and Sn_DPORTR with the group's MAC address, IP address and port before OPEN; the chip handles IGMP itself.

An IPRAW socket carries one IPv4 protocol, chosen in Sn_PROTOR; TCP, UDP and IPv6 are not available this way. Received packets carry a 6-byte header: peer IP (4) and length (2). With Sn_PROTOR = ICMP the chip stops answering pings itself and hands ping requests to the socket. Data above MSS must be split by the host.

Socket 0 in MACRAW mode sends and receives whole Ethernet frames. Sn_MR[MF] keeps only broadcast, multicast and own-address frames; Sn_MR2 can drop broadcast, multicast and IPv6 frames. Frames meant for other open sockets are not delivered; ARP and ping requests are delivered and still answered by the chip. Each received frame has a 2-byte length header. Frames shorter than 60 bytes are padded with zeros on transmit.

Without opening a socket, SLCR[ARP] or SLCR[PING] sends an ARP or ping request to the IP in SLPIPR, retrying every SLRTR up to SLRCR times. A reply sets SLIR[ARP] (and puts the peer MAC in SLPHAR) or SLIR[PING]; running out of retries sets SLIR[TIMEOUT]. One command at a time; PINGSEQR and PINGIDR set the ping sequence number and ID, and the sequence number does not step by itself.

ARP and ping requests repeat every RTR (or Sn_RTR, SLRTR) until answered or the count passes RCR. TCP retransmission of SYN, FIN or data doubles the interval each time, capped once it would pass 65535 units, and raises Sn_IR[TIMEOUT] after Sn_RCR retries; a TCP socket then closes.

MR[PB] stops ping replies, MR2[NOTCPRST] stops TCP resets to closed ports and MR2[UDPURB] stops ICMP port-unreachable replies, which hides the device from port scans. IR[CONFLICT] reports another host using the same IP. NETLCKR locks GAR, SUBR, SHAR and SIPR against writes.
With MR2[WOL] and PHYCR1[WOL] both 1 the chip watches for a UDP magic packet and sets IR2[WOL], which can drive INTn through IMR2.

MR[PPPoE] turns on PPPoE. PHAR holds the server MAC, PSIDR the session ID and PMRUR the MRU (at most 1472, set before OPEN). PTIMER sets the LCP echo interval in 25 ms steps and PMAGIC the byte repeated four times as the LCP magic number. IR[PPPTERM] reports a terminate from the server.

SYS_CLK runs at 100 MHz by default and at 25 MHz when MR2[CLKSEL] = 1 (after unlocking CLKLCKR with 0xCE), during a PHY reset, or in PHY power-down. After any switch the host waits for the clock to settle (TFI, TLF, TPRST).

Unlock PHYLCKR with 0x53, write the speed and duplex (or auto-negotiation) into PHYCR0, reset the PHY with PHYCR1[RST], wait TPRST and for the link, check PHYSR0, then lock PHYLCKR by writing any other value. A new PHYCR0 setting takes effect only after a PHY reset. Against a partner without auto-negotiation the PHY links by parallel detection, which can leave the two ends at different duplex.
Auto-MDIX works only with auto-negotiation on (PHYCR0 in auto mode), using a symmetric transformer. With a fixed mode a crossover cable is needed unless the partner does auto-MDIX.

Unlock PHYLCKR, set PHYCR1[PWDN], lock again and wait TPRST: the PHY stops and SYS_CLK drops to 25 MHz, taking the supply to 10 mA typ. To wake, clear PWDN the same way, then wait TPRST and TLF for the clock to return to 100 MHz.

The internal PHY's registers sit behind an MDC/MDIO controller. Put the register address in PHYRAR; for a write load PHYDIR and set PHYACR = 0x01, for a read set PHYACR = 0x02 and read PHYDOR; PHYACR returns to zero when done. PHYDIVR sets the management clock. Example: BMCR at 0x00 (bit 15 is a software reset), BMSR at 0x01 (bit 2 is link).

3V3D and 3V3A take 3.3 V. The 1.2 V core rails 1V2D and 1V2A come from the chip's own regulator at 1V2O, which can deliver 150 mA, needs 3.3 µF on its output and a ferrite bead, feeds 1V2D and 1V2A on separate paths, and serves nothing else.

Either a 25 MHz crystal across XSCI and XSCO with an external 1 MΩ feedback resistor and load capacitors, or a 25 MHz oscillator at 1.2 V levels into XSCI with XSCO left open. The recommended crystal is ±30 ppm, 7 pF maximum shunt capacitance, 500 µW drive, 12 pF load, ±3 ppm per year aging.
The line interface takes 1:1 transformers with 350 µH on both the transmit and receive windings. Asymmetric and symmetric transformer types both apply; auto-MDIX uses the symmetric type.
LNKn, SPDn, DPXn, ACTn and COLn are active-low outputs with pull-ups that show link, 100 Mbps speed, full duplex, activity (flashing on traffic) and collision in either host mode.
